rules.unenforced: No automation checks whether test recovery values match server-saved defaults; requires semantic knowledge of per-field server state unavailable to static analysis
No forbidden-pattern or lint bans direct getAttribute('aria-invalid') in specs; enforceable by adding a forbidden-patterns entry forcing use of polling page-object helpers

Task classification is judgment — no hook verifies the agent chose the correct matrix row. browsertool-gate enforces frontmatter-consistency, not classification correctness.

First-output announcement is un-gateable (no hook determines 'first output of a browser-interacting session'). BrowserTool frontmatter existence is deliberately fail-open (check-browsertool.mjs:172-175). BrowserToolJustification validator claimed by rule text does not exist.
Switch logging is activity-log discipline. No hook verifies [BROWSER-SWITCH] rows exist. Switch budget (>=2 YELLOW, >=3 RED) is retrospective /final-q + /audit concern, not a structural gate.

Chrome websocket drop is a runtime event. No hook detects connection drops — PreToolUse fires before tool calls, not in response to tool failures. Drop logging and HALT-on-chrome-only are behavioral directives with no structural enforcement.

Mandate to grep Table 2 BEFORE answering is a temporal-process requirement — no hook can verify an agent consulted a specific file before formulating a response. Companion defenses (todo-injection-gate, verify-no-forbidden) catch downstream output on targeted paths but do not enforce the consultation mandate itself.
